examples.en: It's convenient to leave tax filing to a tax accountant.
I booked a consultation at the tax accountant's office.
I found a tax accountant when I started my own business.
The tax accountant checked the documents carefully for me.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 세무사와 계약해서 장부를 관리해요.
examples.en: Our shop has a contract with a tax accountant who manages our books.
I asked how much a tax accountant would cost.

explain: 세금 신고와 납부를 도와주는 전문가를 말해요. 가게나 회사를 하는 사람은 '세무사 사무실'에 일을 맡기는 경우가 많아요. 돈의 흐름을 정리하고 검토하는 일을 하는 '회계사'와는 하는 일이 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a tax accountant as I start my shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움이 필요해서 전문가를 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you look for an expert to help you.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for a tax accountant

phrases.example: 세금 문제는 세무사와 상담하는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's good to consult a tax accountant about tax issues.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신고 전에 물어보고 의논할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking advice before filing.

phrases.en: He is preparing for the tax accountant exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 얻기 위한 자격 시험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the qualification exam for the job.

explain_en: This is the professional who helps with tax filing and payment. People who run shops or companies often leave the work to a '세무사 사무실'. It is a bit different from a '회계사' (accountant), who focuses on organizing and reviewing financial records.

examples.en: The teacher explained the rules in detail.
I wrote down the travel schedule in detail.
Please check the receipt item by item.

examples.ko: 그는 사고 상황을 세세히 기억하고 있어요.
examples.en: He remembers the details of the accident clearly.
If you go over every little detail, it's tiring.
The instructions explain how to use it in great detail.

explain: '세밀히'처럼 꼼꼼하다는 뜻이지만, 하나하나 작은 항목까지 빠뜨리지 않는 느낌이 더 강해요. 설명하다·적다·기억하다처럼 내용을 풀어내는 말과 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Please read the contract terms in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세세히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '세세하게'도 아주 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '세세히'; '세세하게' is also very common in speech.

phrases.example: 그날 있었던 일을 지금도 세세히 기억해요.
phrases.en: I still remember what happened that day in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 부분까지 빠짐없이 기억하고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you remember even the small parts without missing anything.

phrases.example: 점원이 사용 방법을 세세히 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: The clerk told me in detail how to use it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 자세한 내용을 하나하나 말해 줄 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when someone tells you the details one by one.

explain_en: Like '세밀히' it means thorough, but it stresses not skipping any small item one by one. It often goes with verbs of laying out content, such as 설명하다, 적다 and 기억하다.

examples.en: My application was approved yesterday.
The new plan was approved at the meeting.
I will contact you right away when the loan is approved.

examples.ko: 승인된 사람만 이 문으로 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only approved people can enter through this door.
I am upset because my leave was not approved.
I got a text saying the payment was approved.

explain: '승인되다'는 허락하는 사람이 따로 있을 때 써요. 대출·휴가·결제처럼 윗사람이나 기관이 결정하는 일에 어울려요. 허락하는 쪽에서는 '승인하다'를 써요. '허락되다'는 일상 말이고, '승인되다'는 서류와 앱 알림에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 제 신청서는 지금 승인 대기 중이에요.
phrases.en: My application is waiting for approval now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 서류에서 아직 결과를 기다릴 때 자주 보이는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in apps and forms when the result is still pending.

phrases.en: The payment was not approved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락이 나지 않았다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that permission was not given.

phrases.en: Taking photos is not allowed here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류보다 일상 이야기에 어울리는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that fits everyday talk better than paperwork.

explain_en: '승인되다' fits things decided by someone with authority, such as loans, leave, or payments. The person or body giving permission uses '승인하다'. '허락되다' is more everyday, while '승인되다' appears more in documents and app notifications.

dis.h: formally approved after review, plan or request
gh: officially licensed by authorities, e.g. a school

p.n: Approved through a formal process versus simply allowed by someone.

en: to newly set up (a department, office, school)

examples.en: The city is setting up a new children's library.
The company newly established a marketing department this year.
The school is planning to start a new club.

examples.ko: 지하철 노선을 신설하는 데 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to build a new subway line.

examples.ko: 정부가 새로운 지원 제도를 신설할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The government is going to set up a new support system.

examples.ko: 식당은 인기가 많아서 지점을 하나 더 신설했어요.
examples.en: The restaurant was so popular that it opened one more branch.

explain: 기관, 부서, 제도, 노선을 새로 만든다는 뜻이라 공식적인 글과 뉴스에 많이 나와요. '만들다'는 물건에도 쓰지만 '신설하다'는 조직이나 제도에만 써요. 반대말은 '폐지하다'예요.

phrases.en: The company set up a new customer center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직이나 부서를 새로 만들 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical pairing for creating a new organization or department.
phrases.en_equiv: to set up a new department

phrases.en: The city plans to create a new bus route.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 만들 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a plan to create something.

phrases.en: The school created a new club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 일상 표현이지만 공식적인 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday expression with less formality.

explain_en: It means creating a new organization, department, system or route, and it shows up a lot in formal writing and news. 만들다 works for objects too, but 신설하다 is only for organizations and systems. The opposite is 폐지하다, to abolish.

en: to entrust; to leave; to commit

examples.en: The boss delegated some tasks to the team leader.
We decided to leave the contract matter to the lawyer.
I was busy, so I had a friend handle the paperwork submission.

examples.ko: 권한을 위임하면 일이 더 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If you delegate authority, work gets done faster.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 혼자 하지 말고 위임해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't do everything alone; try delegating.

examples.ko: 결정을 위임한 사람이 결과에 책임져야 해요.
examples.en: The person who handed off the decision must answer for the result.

explain: '맡기다'와 비슷하지만 '위임하다'는 일뿐 아니라 그 일을 결정할 권한까지 넘긴다는 느낌이 있어요. 회사, 법률, 행정 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 이때 서류로 만든 증명이 '위임장'이에요. 일상에서 친구에게 부탁할 때는 '맡기다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I delegated the authority to decide to the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: '권한'과 함께 쓰면 일뿐 아니라 결정할 힘도 넘긴다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '권한' it is clear that not only the work but also the power to decide is handed over.

phrases.en: I was given authority over the contract by the CEO.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위임하는 사람이 아니라 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving the authority.

phrases.en: I left this task to my colleague.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요. 권한까지 넘기는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday word, with less of the sense of handing over authority.

explain_en: Like '맡기다' (to leave something to someone), but 위임하다 hands over the authority to decide along with the task. It appears in business, law, and administration, and the written proof is a '위임장'. For asking a friend a favor, '맡기다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 우리는 모든 문제를 일괄적으로 해결하는 방식을 택했어요.
examples.en: We chose to resolve all the problems in one go.
I'll accept the applications all together in one batch.

examples.ko: 일괄적인 규칙을 모든 학년에 적용하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to apply one blanket rule to every grade.

examples.ko: 요금을 일괄적으로 올리면 불만이 클 거예요.
examples.en: If you raise the fees across the board, people will be very unhappy.

examples.ko: 파일 이름을 일괄적으로 바꾸는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to rename files all at once.

examples.ko: 사람마다 상황이 다른데 일괄적으로 처리하면 곤란해요.
examples.en: Everyone's situation is different, so handling it all the same way is a problem.

explain: '일괄적으로'처럼 부사로, '일괄적인'처럼 명사 앞에서 써요. '한꺼번에'는 일상 말이고 '일괄적'은 규칙이나 처리 방식을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '일률적'은 똑같이 적용한다는 점에, '일괄적'은 한데 묶어서 처리한다는 점에 무게가 있어요.

phrases.en: I'll process the applications all together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 건을 한데 묶어 처리한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, meaning handling many items bundled together.

phrases.example: 일괄적인 처리 방식이라 시간이 적게 걸려요.
phrases.en: It's a bundled way of processing, so it takes less time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓸 때는 '-인'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -인 when it modifies a noun.

phrases.en: Please submit the documents all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일괄적으로'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 일괄적으로 but far more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used as an adverb ('일괄적으로') or before a noun ('일괄적인'). '한꺼번에' is everyday speech, while '일괄적' suits rules and ways of handling things. '일률적' leans toward applying things identically, whereas '일괄적' leans toward bundling things together.

en: to be written; to be filled in; to be drawn up

examples.en: Documents are drawn up on a computer.
The contract was drawn up yesterday.
This text was written in Korean.
Please check the written report.
Once the application is filled in, I will accept it.
There is a box that has not been filled in yet.

explain: 서류, 보고서, 계약서처럼 공식적으로 써서 만드는 글에 써요. 일기나 편지처럼 가볍게 쓴 글은 '쓰여 있다'가 더 자연스러워요. 내가 쓰면 '작성하다'예요.

phrases.en: Please email the document that has been filled out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작성된'은 이미 만들어진 서류를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a document already written.

phrases.en: The report is written in English.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 지금 그 상태라는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 있다' describes the current state of the document.

phrases.en: The application has not been filled out yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류가 아직 만들어지지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the document has not yet been prepared.

explain_en: It is used for texts written up in an official way, such as documents, reports and contracts. For lighter writing like diaries and letters, '쓰여 있다' sounds more natural. When you write it yourself, use '작성하다'.

dis.h: a whole document is drawn up
gh: stated or listed in a document, formal
gets written down; plain everyday word
shown by label or spelling notation

p.n: Entered applies to details in a document, not a whole one.

en: once again; for a second time (formal)

examples.en: The teacher told us to check once more.
The company expressed its apology once again.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 재차 물어봤지만 대답이 없었어요.
examples.en: I asked that person a second time, but there was no answer.

examples.ko: 점원이 재차 같은 질문을 해서 조금 당황했어요.
examples.en: The clerk asked the same question again, and I was a bit flustered.
The boss stressed it again.
He tried again but failed once more.

explain: 재차는 이미 한 일을 두 번째로 또 한다는 느낌의 말이에요. 말보다 글이나 뉴스, 공식적인 말투에서 많이 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '또', '다시'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The president stressed the importance of safety once again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 이미 한 말을 다시 강하게 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in the news when repeating a point with emphasis.

phrases.en: The teacher told me to check again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: My friend changed the appointment time again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구와 편하게 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for casual conversation with friends.

explain_en: 재차 means doing something a second time, after it was already done once. It fits writing, news and formal speech. With friends, Koreans say 또 or 다시 instead.

gh: redo or restart from the beginning
casual: another time, one more occurrence

p.n: The original is formal and written; the replacement is neutral and spoken.

examples.ko: 회사는 밤새 작업해서 공장 가동을 정상화했어요.
examples.en: The company worked through the night and restored normal factory operation.

examples.ko: 하루빨리 서비스를 정상화해야 고객이 불편하지 않아요.
examples.en: We have to restore the service quickly so customers aren't inconvenienced.

examples.ko: 직원들이 힘을 모아 운행을 정상화하려고 노력했어요.
examples.en: The staff joined forces and tried to restore normal service.

examples.ko: 정부는 두 나라의 관계를 정상화하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to normalize relations between the two countries.

examples.ko: 시스템을 정상화하는 데 두 시간쯤 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took about two hours to get the system back to normal.

examples.ko: 누가 이 업무를 정상화해 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Who can get this work back on track?

explain: '~을/를 정상화하다'처럼 목적어가 있을 때 써요. 저절로 원래대로 돌아오는 상황은 '정상화되다'를 써서 짝으로 구분하면 돼요.

phrases.en: We have to restore the service first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일이나 목표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state something that has to be done.

phrases.en: The staff are trying to get operations back to normal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 걸리는 일을 해 나가는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an effort that takes time and is still going on.

phrases.example: 시스템을 정상으로 되돌리는 데 두 시간이 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: It took two hours to get the system back to normal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자어 대신 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way of saying it without the Sino-Korean word.

explain_en: Use it with an object, as in '~을/를 정상화하다'. When something returns to normal by itself, use '정상화되다' instead, so learn them as a pair.

examples.en: The report hasn't been submitted yet.
The documents were submitted to the school yesterday.
Once the application is submitted, a confirmation email is sent.

examples.ko: 제출된 과제는 다시 고칠 수 없어요.
examples.en: A submitted assignment can't be edited again.
Several written opinions are being submitted.

examples.ko: 모든 답안이 시간 안에 제출돼야 해요.
examples.en: All answer sheets must be submitted in time.

explain: 내는 사람이 주어이면 '제출하다', 낸 서류가 주어이면 '제출되다'를 써요. '내다'보다 공식적이라서 과제, 서류, 신청서, 보고서와 잘 어울려요. 친구에게 물건을 줄 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Please check whether the documents have been submitted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내야 하는 서류나 과제가 들어왔는지 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when checking whether required documents or assignments have come in.

phrases.en: The application must be submitted by Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어야 해요'로 꼭 해야 하는 일을 말해요. 기한과 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-a/eoya haeyo' states something that must happen. It often goes with deadlines.

phrases.en: I handed my report in to the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제출하다'보다 쉽고 일상적이에요. 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is simpler and more everyday than '제출하다'. The subject is the person handing it in.

explain_en: When the person handing it in is the subject, use '제출하다'; when the document itself is the subject, use '제출되다'. It is more official than '내다' and goes with assignments, documents, applications, and reports. It is not used for giving a friend an item.

examples.ko: 회사는 공장 증설을 올해 안에 끝낼 거예요.
examples.en: The company will finish expanding the factory this year.
The students were happy about the news that more buses would be added.

examples.ko: 증설 공사 때문에 길이 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: The roads are very congested because of the expansion work.

examples.ko: 병원은 병실 증설이 꼭 필요하다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The hospital said adding more patient rooms is absolutely necessary.

examples.ko: 서버 증설을 하고 나서 접속이 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: After the servers were added, connecting got faster.
The plan to add subway capacity was announced yesterday.

explain: '증설'은 공장·서버·병실처럼 이미 있는 시설에 더 붙일 때 써요. 처음 짓는 건 '건설'이나 '설립', 수나 양이 많아지는 건 '증가'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The hospital started its expansion construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시설을 더 붙이는 공사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for construction that adds to existing facilities.

phrases.en: The hospital announced a plan to add more rooms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 늘릴 계획을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for plans to add capacity in the future.

phrases.en: Thanks to the server expansion, the site got faster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터 설비를 늘릴 때도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also commonly used for adding computer equipment.

explain_en: 증설 is for adding more to a facility that already exists, such as a factory, server, or ward. Building something new is 건설 or 설립, and a plain rise in number or amount is 증가.

examples.ko: 특허 출원 서류를 다음 주에 내요.
examples.en: I'm submitting the patent application documents next week.

examples.ko: 상표 출원을 하려면 비용이 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to file a trademark application?

examples.ko: 출원 결과는 몇 달 뒤에 나와요.
examples.en: The result of the application comes out in a few months.

examples.ko: 출원이 늦어져서 다른 회사가 먼저 등록했어요.
examples.en: Our filing was late, so another company registered it first.
This design is already being applied for.

examples.ko: 출원 전에 아이디어를 공개하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't make your idea public before filing.

explain: 특허, 상표, 디자인 같은 권리를 정식으로 신청할 때 써요. '특허 출원', '상표 출원'처럼 정해진 말과 같이 나오는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I submitted the patent application form today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출원할 때 내는 서류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The document you submit when filing an application.

phrases.en: You have to file a trademark application first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출원하다'를 명사 형태로 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun-based way to say 'to file an application'.

phrases.en: The filing period ends next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청할 수 있는 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time window in which you can apply.

explain_en: It is used when formally applying for rights such as a patent, trademark or design. It often appears in set pairings like '특허 출원' and '상표 출원'.
